 Ilia Topuria’s orbital fractures were ‘half a millimeter’ away from being career ending
 by Ryan Harkness Nov 17, 2026, 10:52 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Aleksandre Topuria (R) assists his brother, Georgia’s Ilia Topuria (C), as they leave after losing the lightweight title bout against US fighter Justin Gaethje during the “UFC Freedom 250” mixed martial arts event on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC, early morning on June 15, 2026. (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images) AFP via Getty Images Ryan Harkness breaks down daily mixed martial arts (MMA) news, providing unique context to stories that only 15 years of obsessing over the sport can provide, having worked for FOX Sports, Yahoo! Sports, UPROXX, MSN, Bleacher Report, HDNet and CagePotato, among others, before joining MMAmania.com in 2017. Ilia Topuria really meant it when he said his brother saved his career by throwing in the towel during their UFC White House fight against Justin Gaethje.
 Topuria took tremendous damage during his fight with Gaethje, breaking his nose and both orbitals across four rounds. Leading into the fifth round, Topuria’s older brother Aleksandre (himself a UFC fighter) made the call to stop the fight.
 In previous interviews, Topuria credited his brother with saving his career. And now in a new interview with La Gazzetta Georgia, he explained just how close he came to getting retired from the sport by Gaethje.
 “I don’t think I would have lost my eye sight, they would have managed to restore most of my vision after surgeries,” he said of the damage he took. “However, the problem would have been that I could never fight again. When your orbital bones are fractured and you undergo surgery, they insert titanium plates to repair them. Once those plates are in place, you can never take another punch to that area. I narrowly avoided surgery by half a millimeter.”

 Related
 Justin Gaethje shuts down Ilia Topuria immediate rematch: ‘He quit twice’ 
 “God saved me, and my brother saved my right eye,” he concluded.
 Topuria is now preparing for a return to action in April 2027, although it’s unclear who he’ll fight next. There’s a lot of money in an immediate rematch against Justin Gaethje, although the new lightweight champion has made it clear he’s not interested. More willing to fight Topuria is Paddy “The Baddy” Pimblett, a man who has been in a feud with “El Matador” for years.
 Whoever it will be, they’ve now seen that Ilia Topuria is mortal and can be defeated. How Topuria will bounce back from that reality remains to be seen, but we’re kind of hoping for his sake that the UFC doesn’t convince Gaethje to accept an immediate rematch.
